paper.title: BlockCopy-Based Operators for Evolving Efficient Wind Farm Layouts

same_lineage_public_assets.role: released Kusiak evaluator and exact 2014 Competition 1/3 XML lineage
same-author implementation description and conflict evidence; no optimizer code

paper_source_conflicts: The paper says an invalid copied turbine is simply not placed, while the same-author thesis says it is randomly relocated within the target block.
The two Weibull-k ranges printed for 2014 Competition 1 and 3 are opposite the ranges in the official XML files identified by dimensions and counts.
The paper wind-rose caption says 15 bins, while the equations, thesis and public evaluator use 24 sectors of 15 degrees.
The thesis prose prints interest r=0.3, while the paper equation and released evaluator use r=0.03.
The paper reports a (5,10)-ES but omits a complete executable survivor and parent-pairing lifecycle.
missing_information: author BlockCopy optimizer source and random states
completion_decisions: Use the paper-authority omit-invalid-copy rule and record the thesis conflict.
Use official XML identity, arrays, dimensions, counts and obstacles for Competition 1 and 3.
Use the released 24-sector evaluator and Kusiak arrays already audited under T03.
Use r=0.03 from the target paper and source.
Use conventional (5,10) comma-ES semantics with best-five offspring survival, uniform parent sampling and distinct crossover parents.
Use continuous uniform feasible initialization, uniform fixed-count repair and deterministic stable tie resolution.
Implement only the four BlockCopy-containing target methods; exclude TDA and perturbation-only comparison baselines.
Use exact algebraic cone reformulation, lookup-integrated Weibull power, incremental changed-coordinate wake updates and persistent all-core execution.

decision_variables.resolution: 2N continuous Cartesian coordinates for fixed N=100,100,220,710

encoding_and_decoder.resolution: direct coordinates partitioned into the paper's approximately 1km BlockCopy grids

objective_and_direction.resolution: minimize expected energy cost per kWh with fixed count

constraints_and_repair.resolution: rectangular boundary, open rectangular obstacles, pairwise distance >=8R; invalid copy omitted; uniform purge/add restores count

wake_power_cost_or_coupled_model.resolution: released Kusiak/Jensen cone, RSS deficit, direction Weibull quadrature, linear/rated 1.5MW curve and target economics

wind_and_scenario_sampling.resolution: 24 direction sectors; two Kusiak resources and exact Competition 1/3 XML arrays

initialization.resolution: uniform continuous rejection subject to boundary, obstacle and spacing constraints

update_order.resolution: (1+1) stable non-worse acceptance; (5,10) best-five offspring comma survival; BlockCopy source/target then repair

parameters.resolution: paper block grids and counts; equal Both operator probability; random perturbation size 10; fixed 8R spacing

metrics_and_repeats.resolution: four target methods by four problems by 30 runs, 2000 FES each; energy-cost statistics, timings, worker receipts and science hashes

scope.claim_boundary: source-backed flexible academic reproduction of four BlockCopy methods and all four native problems; not author optimizer source, random stream or exact-number replay
